teaser: A Request for Comments: two key pairs so a reader cannot write, sealed files only named people can open, and fourteen questions for reviewers.
core_idea: An sgit vault's read key is symmetric, so anyone who holds it and can write to the store can author history clients accept; turning the read key into a public key does not fix that, but two key pairs do, giving a native PKI vault mode where readers cannot write, hosts cannot forge and write-only depositors become possible, while an optional sealed-files layer encrypts chosen files to named people's public keys with the private key held in a file, an ssh key, hardware or a remote service that logs and approves each decryption; both share a first step, a writer signature on today's vaults, and nothing is built until reviewers have answered fourteen questions.

nodes.label: One symmetric read key
nodes.summary: PBKDF2 derives a read key that encrypts everything and a write key only the server checks.

nodes.label: Whoever can read can forge
nodes.summary: A read-key holder who can write to the store, such as the host or a mirror, can author history.

nodes.label: One key pair is not enough
nodes.summary: The private half yields the public half, and decrypting with a public key is signing; two pairs work.

nodes.label: A writer signature first
nodes.summary: An Ed25519 key from a third derivation path signs refs and index on today's vaults.

nodes.label: Native PKI vault mode
nodes.summary: A read pair and a write pair; a data key sealed to the read public key; signed heads.

nodes.label: The write-only depositor
nodes.summary: Can add content readers open, cannot read: append to an inbox branch.

nodes.label: Sealed files
nodes.summary: An age v1 inner envelope seals chosen files to named people's public keys, on any vault.

nodes.label: Where the private key lives
nodes.summary: A key file, an ssh key, hardware, or a remote service that logs and approves each unwrap.

nodes.label: Writers can replace blindly
nodes.summary: Sealing needs only public keys, so integrity needs signed envelopes and author rules.

nodes.label: Known shapes
nodes.summary: Tahoe-LAFS, Hypercore, git-crypt, SOPS, age and HPKE (RFC 9180).

nodes.label: Fourteen questions
nodes.summary: Where an outside view would most change the design, before anything is built.

quotes.text: Add a second key pair for reading, and every property falls out.
quotes.why: The correction to the obvious idea.

quotes.text: its hard part is not the cryptography but downgrade resistance
quotes.why: Where the writer signature's real work is.
